title: DReX: Accurate and Scalable Dense Retrieval Acceleration via Algorithmic-Hardware Codesign
problem: Approximate nearest-neighbor search (ANNS) used in RAG dense retrieval is dataset-specific and inherently low-recall, causing irrelevant or incomplete context to degrade LLM generation quality. Exact nearest-neighbor search is too compute- and bandwidth-intensive for conventional processors.
motivation: As RAG systems grow to handle trillion-token datastores, retrieval latency, accuracy, and energy directly bottleneck time-to-first-token and generation quality for LLM applications.
method: DReX combines two hardware tiers: in-DRAM logic performs early filtering by comparing query vectors against embedding centroids to eliminate distant candidates without moving full vectors off-chip, and an outside-DRAM near-memory accelerator then executes exact k-NN search on the filtered, much smaller candidate set. The in-DRAM filter exploits processing-in-memory (PIM) capabilities of commodity DRAM to compute approximate distance bounds, bypassing DRAM-to-processor transfers for the bulk of vectors. This two-stage pipeline minimizes off-chip data movement while guaranteeing exact retrieval on the survivors.
key_novelty: Using in-DRAM logic for coarse vector filtering combined with a near-memory accelerator for exact search, eliminating the recall-versus-speed tradeoff of ANNS without bulk off-chip data movement.
contributions: Dataset-agnostic dense retrieval scheme that avoids ANNS approximation errors entirely.
In-DRAM early-filter mechanism that uses PIM logic to compute distance bounds and discard far-away embeddings before DRAM-to-processor transfer.
Near-memory accelerator for exact k-NN search on the filtered candidate set, minimizing off-chip bandwidth.
End-to-end RAG evaluation showing 6.2-7x reduction in time-to-first-token versus state-of-the-art ANNS-based retrieval.

metrics.speedup: 6.2-7x reduction in time-to-first-token vs. state-of-the-art ANNS mechanism
metrics.area: reasonable area and power overhead in memory subsystem (exact numbers not stated in abstract)

limitations: Recall and latency benefits depend on the filtering selectivity of the in-DRAM stage, which may vary with embedding distribution; detailed area/power numbers and comparison to GPU baselines are not stated in the abstract.
primary_theme: near-memory exact dense retrieval for RAG
